exact_statement: For every integer a>=1 and every first-positive selector comb with arbitrary repeated stopping and terminal labels chosen from two distinct nonempty unsigned characters chi_A,chi_B on an independent uniform data cube (A and B may overlap), the explicit coherent max-index output law Q_F from physical suffix means is normalized and has complete ideal cost CE(P_F,Q_F)=H(F)<=C_* I_sel(F), C_*=4+2/(e ln 2)<41/8, with no boundary-retention admission. A finite output prefix code has expected length at most (41/8) I(F). Passive pushforward of the old uniform-mask Kraft law is insufficient: on the terminal-only switch its common output mass is (1-4^(-a))/3, its cross-entropy has liminf at least log2(3), and I_sel=a2^(-a) tends to zero. For any disjoint Boolean seed h and complete seed reference Q_h, the product reference has cost CE_F+CE(P_h,Q_h), retaining the entire arbitrary seed debt. This is a selector-only cost repair, not an improved total-FEI bound for the comb class, whose raw transcript already costs <4<=4I(F).
